evidence_cards.content: The process of overriding a device status shall not affect the status of any other device.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that an operator’s override action during exception handling (e.g., Operational Override) is isolated to the targeted device and does not disrupt or alter the state of unrelated devices — supporting safe continuation of sequence without side effects.

evidence_cards.content: Each control command that is processed must be validated against the secured safety rules... For example, if the operator issues a command to open the south gate while the north gate is open, the RLCS software will determine that opening the south gate cannot occur when the north gate is open, and will give an indication that the operation cannot be completed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Demonstrates that even operator-initiated overrides are subject to interlock validation; thus, an on-demand command issued via Operational Override may still be blocked by safety rules — implying potential halt or rejection rather than automatic resumption.

evidence_cards.content: Commands are only forwarded from superior units to inferior ones. This prevents a lower level unit from changing the state of a device which is controlled by either a higher level unit, or by a peer unit.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes hierarchical control constraints — meaning an operator’s override command must originate from a sufficiently privileged unit (e.g., TSU/FCU), and if issued from an inferior unit, it may be ignored or rejected, affecting whether the sequence can resume.
